prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you put ketchup on a hot dog in the city of Chicago. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, distinguished members of the Committee,

I come before you today not as a criminal, but as a man who once, in a moment of weakness, reached for the wrong condiment.

I will not hide behind the Fifth. I stand before you an open book. Yes, I have squeezed. Yes, it was red. Yes, it was tomato-based. But I ask this Committee to consider the context of the times.

*[dramatically pours a glass of water, drinks]*

I was young. I was hungry. I had wandered from the sacred path of celery salt, of sport peppers, of the neon relish that glows like the very lamp of liberty itself. I knew not what I did.

But let me be clear about what I did NOT do. I never named names. I never pressured another citizen to join me in my ketchup-based activities. Whatever I did, I did alone, in shame, in a folding chair, at approximately 2:15 in the afternoon.

*[points finger]*

And I say to this Committee: who among us has not sinned against the poppy seed bun? Who among us can cast the first pickle spear?

I love this city. I love its dogs, dragged through the garden as the Founders intended. And if my testimony here today can prevent even one young person from committing this act,
